explanation: In Greek business and social settings, direct eye contact is expected and read as a sign of honesty, confidence, and genuine engagement; avoiding it can come across as evasive or disinterested. Greece is also often cited as one of the more physically expressive, high-eye-contact cultures in Europe.
local_tip: Maintain steady, natural eye contact during conversation and meetings — looking away too much can be misread as dishonesty or disinterest.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact can feel intimidating; brief glances are generally preferred.
Direct eye contact with elders or superiors can be seen as challenging; younger people often lower their gaze.
Direct eye contact is valued as a sign of sincerity, similar to Greece.
